_meta.source_notes: MSRPs reflect MY2025 base trims approximated from manufacturer sites and automotive press as of late 2025 / early 2026. Ranges are EPA-certified combined unless noted; winter_range_mi is our derated WV estimate (~28% haircut); highway_range_mi is curated for realistic sustained 70-mph driving. City/highway efficiency from EPA fueleconomy.gov. Per-field confidence and methodology are documented at /state-of-the-data — refresh MSRPs quarterly.
_meta.curation_criteria: Selected for relevance to WV buyers: mix of price points, SUV/truck emphasis, reliable dealer presence in WV or bordering states, PHEV options for range-anxious rural buyers, and several long-range luxury BEVs that also serve the used-market shopper.

vehicles.notes: Dominant US EV SUV. Supercharger access. Verify pricing after recent Tesla adjustments.
Efficient sedan, strong Supercharger network.
Most compelling mid-priced BEV SUV for WV market.
Pickup is the top-selling body style in WV. Home-backup power feature is a real selling point.
Extended Range battery (131 kWh) — 320 mi EPA. ~$15k more than Standard Range but real-world WV highway range jumps to ~245 mi. Better fit for long trips.
Longest-range electric truck available. Strong for contractors / fleet use.
Premium adventure truck. Limited WV dealer presence. AALA-exempt (GVWR >8,500 lbs — heavy vehicles not required to disclose parts content).
Large pack option — 135 kWh / 352 mi EPA. AALA-exempt (GVWR >8,500 lbs). $6k step up from Standard for meaningful extra range.
Established Ford dealer network in WV makes service convenient.
Premium with Extended Range 91 kWh pack — 320 mi EPA. Meaningful step up from Select Standard Range for WV drivers who regularly do longer trips.
Class-leading DCFC speed. Assembled in Georgia (Metaplant opened 2024).
Long Range 77.4 kWh pack — 303 mi EPA. Same 800V ultra-fast DCFC. Common step-up trim for WV buyers who want highway range without Tesla pricing.
Shares 800V platform with Ioniq 5. Fast DCFC. Highest US/CA parts content of any EV on this list (MY2025 AALA).
Wind trim with 77.4 kWh Long Range pack — 310 mi EPA. Same 800V platform as Ioniq 5 LR. Still tops the 2025 AALA index at 80% US/CA parts.
Cheapest new BEV option. CHAdeMO DCFC is a drawback (shrinking network). Best for short-range commuters with home charging only.
Larger, more traditional SUV format.
Assembled in Tennessee. Includes 3 years of free Electrify America charging.
Pro S trim with 82 kWh larger battery — 291 mi EPA. TN-assembled. 3 yrs Electrify America included.
GM platform under Honda skin. Strong Honda dealer network in WV. Assembled in Mexico despite Honda branding.
Toyota reliability reputation. Manufactured in Japan — does not qualify for IRA credit.
Excellent WV option: 42 mi electric covers most commutes, gas backup eliminates range anxiety. No DCFC. Assembled in Japan.
Ford dealer ubiquity in WV.
Off-road capable with electric assist. Popular body style in WV; shorter EV-only range.
Most efficient non-Tesla EV. Aerodynamic sedan shape. Assembled in South Korea — 0% US/CA content.
Small premium crossover. Chinese-assembled; does not qualify for IRA credit.
Practical, reliable. Slower DCFC than Kia EV6. Assembled in South Korea.
Flagship 3-row family EV. US-assembled since late 2024. Biggest recent addition to the family-SUV EV segment.
Premium US-assembled EV on GM platform. GM dealer network broad in WV.
Benchmark PHEV efficiency — 52 mpg on gas, 44 mi all-electric. Best-selling PHEV. Japan-assembled, no IRA credit.
Badge-engineered twin of Toyota bZ4X with Subaru AWD. Strong Subaru dealer presence in WV. Japan-assembled, no IRA credit.
Entry-luxury BMW EV sedan. Germany-built, no IRA credit.
Volvo/Geely sub-brand. China-assembled — no IRA credit and subject to import tariffs.
Polarizing design but high mindshare. Highway range derated further than Model Y/3 due to massive frontal area.
Popular luxury PHEV. 40 mi electric covers most commutes; SC-assembled but imported battery keeps it off the IRA credit list.
3-row SUV sibling of R1T. AALA-exempt (GVWR >8,500 lbs).
Large pack variant — 135 kWh / 352 mi EPA. AALA-exempt. $5k step up for meaningful extra range on long trips.
Entry-luxury Mercedes EV SUV. Compact platform, 5-seat. Hungary-assembled — no IRA credit. Slowest DCFC of the Mercedes lineup (100 kW peak).
Mid-tier Mercedes executive EV sedan. Germany-assembled — no IRA credit.
US-assembled at Mercedes' Tuscaloosa plant — IRA-eligible unlike the sedan. Popular mid-size luxury SUV.

charging.connector_dcfc: CCS (Tesla Supercharger access via NACS adapter)

vehicles.notes: EPA range champion of the US market at 512 mi (19-inch wheels). 21-inch wheels drop to 446 mi. Class-leading 19.2 kW onboard charger. Tesla Supercharger access opened in 2024 via Lucid-provided NACS adapter. Used-market relevance: early Air GT depreciation has been steep.

Lucid's first SUV; 3-row seating with optional 6-seat captain's chairs. 400 kW peak DCFC is class-leading — adds ~200 mi in 11 min on a 350 kW+ charger. Native NACS DCFC port, so Superchargers are plug-and-charge. Rare in WV dealer inventory; most sales online-direct.

Mercedes flagship luxury sedan — 390 mi EPA, one of the longest-range German EVs sold in the US. 2025 model uses the upgraded 118 kWh pack (vs 108 kWh in earlier years). German-assembled so no IRA credit even before §30D repeal. Used-market shoppers: early EQS (2022-2023) depreciated heavily, strong used-buyer value.

Tesla flagship sedan, 410 mi EPA. MY2026 price cut to $74,990 before Tesla ceased Model S/X production in April 2026 — dealer and used-market inventory remains active. Highway range in practice typically 290–320 mi (Tesla EPA is known to overstate; WV elevation and cold compound this). Supercharger network access is the main practical advantage.
Model Y Performance — 3.5s 0-60, uprated brakes, lowered suspension, 21-inch wheels. Range drops ~25 mi vs LR due to wheels/motor. Still IRA-eligible (SUV class, under $80k cap).
Model 3 Performance — 2.9s 0-60, track-tuned suspension, adaptive dampers. Just under the $55k sedan IRA cap. Fastest sub-$60k EV sedan on the market.
R1T Dual Motor Performance — 665 hp, 3.5s 0-60, same tow/payload as Standard. AALA-exempt; over $80k truck IRA cap before options.
R1S Dual Motor Performance — 665 hp, 3.5s 0-60 for a 3-row full-size SUV. AALA-exempt; over $80k SUV IRA cap.
Cadillac flagship EV — 200 kWh battery (largest in class), 450 mi EPA range, 750 hp in Velocity Max launch mode. Over the $80k SUV IRA cap. Same Detroit plant as Silverado EV.
Nissan mid-size EV crossover, 87 kWh long-range pack. Slow home-charging (7.2 kW) — plan for overnight. Japan-built, no IRA credit.
Silverado EV twin with Denali trim — premium interior, same 205 kWh pack, 440 mi range. Over the $80k truck IRA cap.
Acuras first EV, built on GM Ultium at Spring Hill alongside Cadillac Lyriq and Honda Prologue. IRA-eligible (US-assembled, under $80k SUV cap).
Stellantis electric muscle car — retuned Fratzonic exhaust audio, 496 hp R/T dual motor AWD. Over the $55k car IRA cap. Canada-assembled.
